battle.name: 羯陵伽戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前265年前後，孔雀王朝的阿育王自摩揭陀沿東海岸南下，攻下印度東部羯陵伽王國的都城，終結其獨立地位。戰役慘烈漫長，孔雀軍以象兵破城、步兵結長矛陣推進。卡面這支埃及長矛並不在此役，但它所代表的那種綁在木杆上的長矛，正是當年攻城與野戰中步兵的標準兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 羯陵伽戰爭是孔雀王朝與印度東部濱海王國羯陵伽之間的一場決定性戰役，交戰地點在今印度奧里薩邦的孟加拉灣沿岸，核心是馬哈納迪河（古稱大王河）三角洲內陸的王都地帶。孔雀一方以摩揭陀為本，首都華氏城，軍隊按五軍體制編成：戰象居中，戰車、騎兵、步兵為輔，另有負責水運與沿河攻擊的水軍。中央直轄的象軍與步卒是主力，各行省總督與受羈縻的地方首領分領兵眾，工兵攜投石、撞柱與填壕器具隨行。阿育王在位初期曾先遣使者與偏師試探，兵事受阻才親率主力南下，決策權高度集中於王本人。羯陵伽一方是有獨立王統的海濱國家，疆域自恆河下游三角洲南抵大王河與海岸，內陸尚有山地邦國與方國；其國力不靠疆域而靠海運，它是紅海周遊記所列的遠方大港之一，輸出棉布、象牙、珍珠與玳瑁，與斯里蘭卡往來密切。軍隊由王軍、方國兵與城邦守備拼成，象兵與步兵為主，守城倚仗磚牆、濠溝、拒馬與海岸地形。兩相比較，孔雀軍總量遠勝，卻在東海岸面對延長的糧道、季風與沼澤；羯陵伽佔地利與守城之便，故此役成了攻方以兵量壓守方地理的典型戰例。
countriesEn: The Kalinga War was a decisive conflict between the Mauryan Empire and Kalinga, an independent maritime kingdom on the eastern seaboard of India. The fighting took place in what is now Odisha, along the Bay of Bengal and inland in the delta of the Mahendra (Mahanadi) river, around the royal capital. On the Mauryan side the base was Magadha, with its capital at Pataliputra, and the army was organised on the five-fold system: war elephants at the centre, with chariots, cavalry and infantry in support, plus a river and coastal fleet used to move troops and supplies. The centrally controlled elephant and foot units formed the core, while provincial governors and client chiefs brought their own contingents, and engineers travelled with the column carrying stone-throwers, battering rams and earth for filling the ditch. Ashoka tested the situation first with envoys and a detached force, and only after that failed did he bring the main army south in person; operational decisions were concentrated in the king himself. Kalinga, by contrast, was a coastal state with its own ruling line, its own trading network and its own fortifications, stretching from the Ganges delta in the north down to the Mahendra and the sea, with hill principalities and feudatories further inland. Its strength came not from territorial size but from the sea: it was one of the far-eastern emporia named in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, exporting cotton cloth, ivory, pearls and tortoiseshell, and it kept close ties with Sri Lanka. Its army combined royal troops, contingents of feudatories and city garrisons, with elephants and infantry as the main elements, and it relied on brick walls, ditches, chevaux-de-frise and coastal terrain to hold its ground. Numerically the Mauryan host was far larger, but deep in the eastern coastal belt it faced a lengthening line of supply, the monsoon and mangrove swamp. Kalinga, holding the advantage of ground and of a fortified capital, had the better chance in the one kind of contest it could choose, and the campaign became a textbook case of an attacker trying to beat a defender with sheer numbers of men.
people: 阿育王（Devanampriya Piyadassi，約前288至前232年在位）是這場戰爭的決定者。他是孔雀王朝第三代君主，祖父旃陀羅笈多、父頻婆娑羅；父死之後的兄弟爭位中他曾被囚於華氏城，得位後除掉競爭者。他在位初期仍以武力擴張，羯陵伽是他最後一場大規模用兵，戰後卻轉向以法（dhamma）治國，晚年不再以戰爭作為手段。他的祖父旃陀羅笈多才是王朝的奠基者：前317年擊敗塞琉古王，西取犍陀羅，據佛教文獻說曾兩度進攻羯陵伽而不能取城；父親頻婆娑羅在南印度與羯陵伽方向也有用兵傳說。羯陵伽國王的名字沒有被任何銘文保存下來，只在佛傳《阿育王傳》與所謂羯陵伽紀中被寫成一位抵抗到底、令孔雀軍付出慘重代價的君主。戰後的秩序重建由一批人推動：主持華氏城結集的目犍連子一族、把佛法帶往斯里蘭卡的大目犍連（Mahinda），以及阿育王派往各省巡行的法特使（dhamma-mahamatra）。此外還有羯陵伽當地的史官（janaka）群體，正是他們為孔雀王記下那場戰爭的經過。戰場底層則是一批不見於銘文的技術兵：馴象師、車夫、攻城工兵與糧秣隊的指揮者，他們的表現決定了攻城與補給能否成立。
peopleEn: Ashoka (Devanampriya Piyadassi, reigning roughly 288 to 232 BCE) was the man who decided this war. He was the third Mauryan ruler, grandson of Chandragupta Maurya and son of Bindusara; after his father's death he was thrown into prison at Pataliputra during the struggle between his brothers and had to remove his rivals once he took the throne. Early in his reign he was still an expansionist, and Kalinga was the last great war of his own making; afterwards he turned to governing through dhamma and no longer treated war as an instrument of policy. His grandfather Chandragupta was the founder of the dynasty: he defeated the Seleucid king in 317 BCE, took Gandhara in the west, and according to the Buddhist narratives attempted the conquest of Kalinga twice without ever taking the capital. His father Bindusara likewise has a tradition of campaigning in the south and against Kalinga. The name of the Kalinga king himself was preserved by no inscription; he survives only in the Buddhist Ashokavadana and the so-called Kalinga chronicle, where he is written as a ruler who resisted to the end and made the Mauryan host pay dearly for its victory. The reordering that followed the war was carried by a different set of men: the line of Moggaliputta Tissa that presided over the council at Pataliputra, Mahinda, who carried the teaching across to Sri Lanka, and the dhamma-mahamatras, the special commissioners Ashoka sent to tour the provinces. There were also the janaka chroniclers of Kalinga, the local historians who wrote down the course of the war for the Mauryan king. Beneath them all stood the technicians whose names no inscription records: the mahouts, the charioteers, the engineers of the siege train and the quartermasters whose competence decided whether the siege and the supply line would hold together.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛是早王朝時期的兵器：青銅矛頭以繩或皮條綁在木杆上，埃及人用它守城垣，也用它收復失地。它並不隨孔雀軍出現在羯陵伽，但同一種形制的長矛正是這場戰爭兩軍步兵的基本裝備。孔雀步兵的典型編法是長矛、弓、短劍與圓盾並帶，長矛用來頂住對方步卒與守軍的壓力，弓在行軍與攻城時提供曲射掩護，盾遮蔽正面；載於《政事論》的孔雀軍械制度把弓、矛、劍、盾按千計配給國王本人與各級部隊，象上的乘員另用鉤矛（aṅkuśa）、短劍與長標槍壓制城頭。攻城除步卒武器外還需投石機、撞柱、填壕用的土袋與草束、雲梯，以及沿河道調動的船隻；孔雀王朝的水軍把兵員與糧秣運過恆河與大王河，減少了長途陸運的負擔。羯陵伽守軍除了裝上青銅或鐵矛頭的直矛，還用弓、投石標槍與標石對付攻城塔；他們的城防器材包括磚牆、濠溝、拒馬、鹿砦與街壘。雙方的象都屬同一技術體系，孔雀象兵以撞擊破門、靠背上的乘員投射武器與投槍壓制城頭，羯陵伽象則多配在城門與城頭陣位，專責反衝。兵器年齡上，羯陵伽之戰前後印度已進入青銅與鐵並用的時代，長矛桿多取竹木，矛頭則從本地冶煉的銅鐵取得。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card belongs to the Early Dynastic period: a bronze head lashed to a wooden shaft with cord or thong, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and to recover lost ground. It did not march with the Mauryan army at Kalinga, but a spear of exactly that form was the basic arm of the infantry on both sides in this war. The standard Mauryan foot soldier carried spear, bow, short sword and round shield together: the spear to hold off enemy foot and defenders, the bow for curved fire on the march and during the siege, the shield to cover the front. The Mauryan stores system described in the Arthashastra issues bows, spears, swords and shields by the thousand to the king himself and to units of every size, while elephant riders used the ankusha, a short sword and long javelins to work the parapets. Beyond the infantryman's own weapons a siege needed stone-throwers, battering rams, earth-filled bags and brush bundles for the ditch, scaling ladders, and boats for river movement; the Mauryan fleet moved men and grain down the Ganges and the Mahendra, sparing the army a long overland haul. The Kalinga defenders matched straight spears with bronze or iron heads, and added bows, javelins and sling-stones against the attacking towers; their fortification material consisted of brick walls, ditches, chevaux-de-frise, abatis and street barricades. The war elephants on both sides belonged to one technological system: the Mauryan elephants were used to batter gates and to bring their riders and javelins up against the wall, while Kalinga elephants were posted at gates and on the ramparts for counter-charge. The point about dates is that India had entered an age of bronze and iron in the centuries around this war: spear shafts were commonly bamboo or hardwood, and the heads were cast from locally smelted copper and iron.
tactics: 作戰大致分成兩個階段。先是外交與偵察：阿育王先遣使者與小股偏師，企圖逼迫羯陵伽讓步，失敗之後才傾力進攻。主力從摩揭陀出發，分東南兩路南下：一路走恆河谷與三角洲，順恆河、馬哈納迪河的水路輸送兵員糧秣；一路沿孟加拉灣北岸陸路行軍，避開沼澤與密林。行軍受季約束縛，冬春乾季是唯一適合長距離進攻的時段，季風雨季既拖慢腳步又讓船隊停擺，因此戰役被拉長成跨越數個作戰季節的持久戰。接戰後，孔雀軍以戰象與重步兵列於前，騎兵分置兩翼，車隊居中或殿後，工兵隨軍備妥填壕與築壘器具；對付城防的做法是先以弓弩與投石壓制城頭，再用象兵與撞柱破門，並在缺口兩側築起射擊台與階梯。攻城同時不忘切斷援軍與糧道，騎兵分遣搜索沿海村鎮，迫守軍分兵，並封鎖河口的船運。守方則倚城垣縱深反擊：以街壘與屋頂射擊消耗進攻者，門後預伏象兵反衝，出城的小股部隊與鄉村游擊專打糧隊，季風水勢則讓壕溝與低地變成天然的護城河。戰後的轉折是戰爭觀念的改變：孔雀王發布詔令，宣布以法取勝、不再以軍力爭鬥，把戰爭轉成銘文、特使與結集傳教的另一條戰線。
tacticsEn: The campaign fell into two broad phases. First came diplomacy and reconnaissance: Ashoka sent envoys and a small detachment in the hope of forcing concessions, and only after that failed did he commit the main effort. The army set out from Magadha in two prongs running south-east: one along the Ganges valley and the delta, moving troops and grain by water down the Ganges and the Mahendra; the other overland along the northern shore of the Bay of Bengal, skirting swamp and forest. The march was governed by the monsoon, and the dry winter and spring season was the only time a long advance was possible, since the rains slowed the column and stopped the river fleet, which stretched the war across several campaigning seasons. At contact the Mauryan order of battle put elephants and heavy infantry in front, cavalry on the wings, chariots in the centre or in the rear, with engineers carrying earth and works for the ditch. Against a walled city the method was to smother the parapet with arrows and stones first, then break the gate with elephants and rams, and to build firing steps and terraces on either side of the breach. Beside the siege, the Mauryans worked to cut help and supplies: cavalry parties swept the coastal villages, forcing the defenders to divide, and the river mouths were closed to shipping. The defenders answered in depth from the walls, spending the attacker on street barricades and roof fire, holding elephants behind the gates for counter-charge, sending out small columns and village bands against the supply trains, and turning the monsoon-fed low ground and the ditches into a natural moat. What followed was a change in the idea of war itself: the Mauryan king published edicts declaring that victory lay in dhamma and that he would no longer contest by force, converting the war into a different front of edicts, special commissioners and the sending out of councils of monks.
data: 關於兵力，現存最接近的量級記載來自孔雀帝國興盛期、略早於此戰的希臘使節梅加斯提尼（經阿里安與斯特拉堡的引文保存）：他描述孔雀王有步兵約六十萬、騎兵三萬、戰車九千、戰象四千，首都華氏城內另有工匠大約四十萬，駐軍約九萬。這些數字是外交場合的誇大陳述，只能當作量級參考，不能當作羯陵伽之戰的實際出動兵力；後世佛史以數十萬步兵、數千騎兵與更多的戰象描述孔雀王的軍隊，同樣帶有文學色彩。傷亡方面，蘭普爾瓦石碑（比哈邦，前一世紀）記述此戰艱苦，提到十萬量級的羯陵伽人陣亡、數萬被俘，另有大量逃散；這是印度傳統的概數寫法，學者普遍不視為可用的精確統計，本卡也不採用任何更精確的數字。年份方面，弗石詔令 XIII 記孔雀王於登基第八年征服羯陵伽，依現代斷代多落在公元前261年前後，另有公元前250年等說法，本卡採公元前265年；月份無任何銘文可考，卡上的十一月是依乾季作戰與圍城時序所作的推定。距離上，華氏城至羯陵伽都城約九百至一千二百公里，橫跨恆河下游與大王河三角洲。城防方面，希蘇帕爾加爾的磚牆一般測得高約十八米、厚約四點八米，周長約一點二公里，外有寬約六米的濠溝與八座城門，是當時已知最宏大的磚砌要塞之一。城內人口、商路吞吐量與兩軍實際傷亡都沒有可靠數字，不作推算。
dataEn: On numbers, the closest surviving statement of scale comes from the Macedonian envoy Megasthenes, who visited the Mauryan state before this war and whose words are preserved by Arrian and Strabo: he describes a royal army of about 600,000 foot, 30,000 cavalry, 9,000 chariots and 4,000 elephants, together with some 400,000 artisans in the city of Pataliputra and a garrison of about 90,000. These are diplomatic exaggerations and can only be used as an order of magnitude, never as the actual force committed at Kalinga. Later Buddhist chronicles describe the Mauryan host with tens of thousands of foot, several thousand cavalry and a still larger number of elephants, in the same literary register. On losses, the Rampurva stone of the first century BCE in Bihar records that the war was hard going and speaks of a hundred thousand of the Kalingas killed, tens of thousands taken captive and many more in flight. That is the Indian convention of round-number expression, and scholars generally refuse to treat it as a usable statistic, so no more precise figures are given here. On dating, Major Rock Edict XIII records that the king conquered Kalinga in the eighth year after his consecration, which most modern chronologies place around 261 BCE, while other estimates give 250 BCE; the date used on this card is 265 BCE. No inscription records the month, and the November shown here is a reconstruction from the dry-season campaigning and the sequence of the siege. As for distance, Pataliputra lies roughly nine hundred to twelve hundred kilometres from the Kalinga capital, spanning the lower Ganges and the Mahendra delta. On fortification, the brick wall at Sisupalgarh is generally measured at about eighteen metres high and four point eight metres thick, with a circuit of some one and a half kilometres, a ditch about six metres wide and eight gates, making it one of the largest brick fortresses then known. Population, port throughput and verified casualty figures for either army simply do not exist, and none are estimated here.
cause: 羯陵伽之所以必須被拿下，是孔雀王朝東進的必然結果。難陀王朝時代的摩揭陀已是北印度的中央集權國家，旃陀羅笈多推翻難陀之後建立孔雀王朝，滅掉的是迦尸、拘薩羅等北印度諸國，東界大致停在恆河與往孟加拉灣分水的支流一帶；羯陵伽是沿海獨立的王國，有自己的王統、自己的海商網絡與自己的城防體系，既不向孔雀朝貢也不接受孔雀的度量衡與稅制，於是成為帝國向東推進時唯一還能整片拒絕整合的地方。佛教文獻把前因寫得更具體：旃陀羅笈多與頻婆娑羅都曾用兵羯陵伽而不能取下都城，最後由阿育王完成；這一說法出自後世文學，學者多視為把王朝的征服史連貫化的敘事，但它至少說明孔雀王朝對羯陵伽的壓力不是一次性的，而是延續了三代人的長期目標。實際觸發戰爭的直接原因沒有留下文字記載，可能與徵稅、駐軍、貿易競爭或羯陵伽對沿岸其他小國的庇護有關，任何一項都屬推測。值得注意的是時機：阿育王剛經歷王位繼承的內部清洗，兄弟相殘的記憶與宗教上的說法都提示他需要一個能證明統治正當性的對外勝利，而羯陵伽的海岸位置也讓一次成功的遠征同時打開通向斯里蘭卡的航路與傳教通道。
causeEn: Kalinga had to be taken because it was the unavoidable consequence of the Mauryan drive eastward. Under the Nandas, Magadha had already become a centralised state in northern India; when Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nandas and founded the dynasty, he destroyed the kingdoms of Kashi and Kosala and pushed the eastern frontier of the empire out to roughly the Ganges and its delta tributaries. Kalinga was a coastal kingdom with its own ruling line, its own network of maritime merchants and its own system of fortification. It neither paid tribute to the Maurya nor accepted its weights, measures and taxes, and it therefore became the one region that could still refuse wholesale integration as the empire moved east. The Buddhist literature makes the background more concrete: both Chandragupta and Bindusara campaigned against Kalinga without ever taking the capital, and Ashoka finished the business. That account comes from later literary hands and is generally read as a tidying of the dynasty's conquest history, but at least it shows that Mauryan pressure on Kalinga was not a single stroke but an objective carried across three generations. The immediate trigger is not recorded anywhere in writing; it may have had to do with taxation, garrisoning, competition over trade, or Kalinga harbouring smaller states along the coast, and each of these remains speculation. The timing deserves notice. Ashoka had just emerged from the blood of the succession, and both the memory of fratricide and the religious argument of the age would have pressed him to win an external victory that legitimised his rule. The coastal position of Kalinga also meant that one successful expedition would open at once a sea route and a corridor of missionary travel towards Sri Lanka.
impact: 此役的直接結果是羯陵伽王國的政治生命終結，卻也把孔雀王朝的性質徹底改掉。弗石詔令 XIII 記孔雀王征服後為羯陵伽人的苦難深感憂傷與悔恨，正是在同一批詔令裡他宣布以法（dhamma）為最高手段：放棄武力爭鬥、禁止以祭祀為名的屠宰、設立法特使巡行各省，並在羯陵伽腹地留下達奧利與喬伽達兩處岩壁詔令，宣告孝親、敬師、禮僧、待婆羅門、寬待奴僕與不殺生。於是孔雀的東方邊界沒有靠城牆守，而是靠一批會講法的官員與僧侶維持。佛教的傳播由此加速：傳統記載的第三次結集在華氏城召開，大目犍連等僧人被派往斯里蘭卡，把佛法帶給那裡的國王，而羯陵伽的海商網絡正是僧侶與經卷東渡的通道之一，傳教團名單中也有專往羯陵伽地區的一支。長期看，這次征服把印度洋的北部海岸拉進同一個政治與商業秩序，羯陵伽的港市後來在佛教傳統中成為東印度與斯里蘭卡之間的信仰橋樑；反過來說，孔雀王朝的權力重心也從北方的恆河流域移向南方與沿海，與南印度諸國的接觸從此更頻繁，這正是後來羯陵伽本地的柯超王朝能以建國以來一百五十三年自居的歷史背景。
impactEn: The immediate outcome of the war was the end of the political life of the kingdom of Kalinga, but it also changed the nature of the Mauryan state itself. Major Rock Edict XIII records that after the conquest the king felt deep sorrow and remorse for the suffering of the Kalingans, and in that same body of edicts he proclaimed dhamma as the highest instrument: abandoning contention by force, ending ritual slaughter, appointing dhamma-mahamatras to travel the provinces, and posting rock edicts in the very heart of Kalinga, at Dhauli and Jaugada, announcing respect for parents and teachers, reverence for monks and brahmins, kindness to servants and people, and the taking of life. The eastern frontier of the empire was henceforth to be held not by walls but by officials and monks who could expound the law. The spread of the Buddhist teaching accelerated with it: according to the received tradition a third council met at Pataliputra, and monks such as Mahinda were sent to Sri Lanka to bring the teaching to its king, Kalinga's maritime network being one of the routes by which monks and texts travelled east, and the list of missions includes one bound for the Kalinga country itself. In the long run the conquest pulled the whole northern shore of the Indian Ocean into a single political and commercial order, and the harbours of Kalinga later served as a bridge of faith between eastern India and Sri Lanka. It also moved the centre of gravity of Mauryan power away from the Ganges plain towards the south and the coast, sharpening contact with the Deccan kingdoms, which is the background against which the later Kalingan ruler Kharavela could claim to have ruled for one hundred and fifty-three years.
result: 勝負是清楚的：孔雀軍攻下羯陵伽王都，王國的政治機構被拆解，地方王統中斷，羯陵伽從獨立的濱海國變成孔雀帝國的一個行省，設法特使與軍事駐紮。這場戰爭沒有留下可核對的兩軍傷亡數字，只有蘭普爾瓦石碑那樣以十萬、數萬概數寫下的記載，因此勝負只能從結果倒推。孔雀王付出的代價不只在兵員，也在士氣與名聲：戰後他放棄以軍力爭鬥的原則，把華氏城的一場結集與多支傳教團的派遣當成新的攻勢，這在冷兵器時代幾乎是前所未有的。對印度與斯里蘭卡而言，這條路帶來的不只是佛法，也帶來了北印度的商品、僧侶與制度，越過孟加拉灣的聯繫自此長期化。對孔雀王朝自身，羯陵伽是它版圖的東端盡頭，此後帝國的重心轉向西北邊界與塞琉古的殘餘勢力，內部的異質性與邊疆距離也開始顯現；公元前232年阿育王去世後，帝國迅速分化，羯陵伽的實際控制隨之鬆脫，但羯陵伽的名號沒有消失：它在後來的佛教經典、斯里蘭卡的地名與族群記憶、以及本地王朝的自我敘述中反覆出現，成為印度史上最長壽的王朝名號之一。
resultEn: The outcome is not in doubt. The Mauryan army took the Kalinga capital, the institutions of the kingdom were broken up, the local ruling line was extinguished, and Kalinga passed from an independent maritime state to a province of the empire, with resident troops and special commissioners. The war left no verifiable casualty figures for either side, only the round-number statements of the Rampurva stone, so the result can only be read backwards from the outcome. What the Mauryan king paid was not only in men but in morale and reputation: after the war he gave up the principle of contesting by force and treated a council at Pataliputra and a set of missions to the south and to Sri Lanka as a new offensive, something almost without precedent in the age of cold weapons. For India and Sri Lanka the road that opened carried not only the teaching but the goods, monks and institutions of northern India, and the connection across the Bay of Bengal became a long one. For the Mauryan state itself, Kalinga was the eastern end of the empire, and from then on its attention turned towards the north-west frontier and the surviving Seleucid power, with the internal diversity of the empire and the sheer distance to its edges becoming more visible. When Ashoka died in 232 BCE the empire broke up quickly and Kalinga's actual control loosened with it, but the name survived: it recurs in the later Buddhist canon, in the place-names and collective memory of Sri Lanka, and in the self-description of Kalingan dynasties, and it remains one of the longest-lived dynastic names in Indian history.
